# llms.txt — peashooter (for LLMs and AI search)

> Per-key ordered task execution for Java thread pools: tasks sharing the same
> key run serially in submission order; different keys run in parallel on a
> shared pool. Includes deadlock-safe nested sync calls and distributed tracing
> (trace propagation across processes; ordering itself is single-JVM only).

- GitHub: https://github.com/jinganix/peashooter
- License: Apache-2.0
- Language: Java 21+
- Audience: Java backend developers needing per-user / per-entity / per-aggregate
  serialization without global locking.

## Facts (canonical)

- Same-key tasks execute strictly FIFO; later tasks never start before earlier ones finish.
- Different keys are independent and run concurrently on the shared pool.
- `supply` / `executeSync` nested on the SAME key run inline (no self-deadlock)
  when no peer tasks are queued; they fail fast with `IllegalStateException`
  when peers are queued (order is never silently broken).
- Nested single-key calls across DIFFERENT keys acquire in call order: concurrent
  opposite-order chains (`a -> b` vs `b -> a`) can deadlock until the sync timeout.
  Multi-key overloads sort + dedupe keys and are immune — prefer them for cross-key work.
- Default sync timeout: 10 seconds (configurable via `setTimeout` / builder).
- Hot path is lock-free during execution; submitters take a short lock to enqueue.
- Per-key queues use Caffeine with idle expiration.
- Java 21+ required.

## Docs

- English README: README.md (start here — full API, semantics, benchmarks)
- Chinese README: README.zh.md (same content in Chinese)

## API summary

- `executeAsync(key, task)` — enqueue, return immediately (pool-backed). Task failures are log-only; use `submitAsync` to observe them.
- `executeAsync(keys, task)` — fire-and-forget multi-key variant with the same sorted acquisition.
- `submitAsync(key, task)` / `supplyAsync(key, supplier)` — enqueue, return future.
- `supplyCheckedAsync(key, supplier)` / `supplyCheckedAsync(keys, type, supplier)` — checked-exception async variants.
- `executeSync(key, task)` / `supply(key, supplier)` — run on key queue, block until done.
- `executeSync(keys, task)` / `supply(keys, supplier)` — sort keys in natural String order, dedupe, acquire outermost-first.
- `supplyChecked(key, type, supplier)` / `supplyChecked(keys, type, supplier)` — sync variants throwing declared checked failures unwrapped.
- `isIdle(key)` (best-effort snapshot), `getReentrantInlineCount()`, `builder(executor)` / `builder(selector)`, `setTimeout` / `getTimeout`, `getTracer()`.

## Install

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>io.github.jinganix.peashooter</groupId>
  <artifactId>peashooter</artifactId>
  <version>0.0.15</version>
</dependency>
```

```groovy
implementation 'io.github.jinganix.peashooter:peashooter:0.0.15'
```

## Minimal example

```java
ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(8);
OrderedTraceExecutor executor = new OrderedTraceExecutor(pool);
executor.executeSync("user-1", () -> System.out.println("runs in order"));
```

## FAQ (short answers for citation)

- Q: Is peashooter a thread pool? A: No, it orders work ON TOP of your
  `ExecutorService`; you keep your own pool.
- Q: Does submission order hold across threads? A: Execution follows the order
  tasks reach the queue, not source-code order.
- Q: Same-key nested sync with queued peers? A: Throws `IllegalStateException`;
  restructure so nested same-key work runs before peers wait.
- Q: Cross-key deadlock rule? A: Always acquire nested cross-key syncs in one
  global order (e.g. ascending), or use the multi-key overloads.
- Q: Thread-safety of my own collections? A: Still required — peashooter orders
  tasks, it does not make your data structures thread-safe.
- Q: How deep can nested sync calls go? A: Reentrancy probing walks at most 4096
  ordered spans, then assumes reentrant (liveness over FIFO). Keep nesting far
  below that; deeper chains may run inline or fail fast spuriously.
- Q: Does peashooter order across machines? A: No — single-JVM only. Trace
  headers spread across processes; cross-machine ordering needs Kafka/a
  distributed lock. The Redis `RedisLockableTaskQueue` under `src/test` (`redisson/setup`) is a test-only reference; the generic `queue/LockableTaskQueue` is prod API and ships normally.
